problem: Existing learned navigation systems count success within a 1 m radius and lack precise goal conditioning, while classical object-pose-estimation pipelines need CAD models, an initially visible object and a map. Neither gives centimeter-level object-relative positioning for docking, inspection or manipulation.
motivation: Downstream tasks such as forklift pallet loading, opening a dishwasher or docking need the robot base at an accurate pose relative to an object, otherwise they fail through collision, out-of-reach or task violation. Human teleoperation data is imprecise, so precise trajectories must come from simulation and model-based planning at large scale.
key_idea: Train an end-to-end transformer on 500k precise, photorealistic simulated trajectories (RGB-D + LiDAR input, reference image + mask + object-centric relative pose as goal) that autoregressively decodes waypoints with residual-refined classification to reach any object at centimeter precision.
insight: The median errors of all ablated variants are comparable, but their long-tail failures differ greatly, so large-scale evaluation is what exposes robustness. Sensor modality matters most: collision rate is 3.8 for the full model versus 25.6 without LiDAR and 17.7 without depth, and 26.2 without the footprint token. The autoregressive decoder beats ACT (5.8 collision rate), and mask tracking helps interpretability more than precision. History matters on the real robot even though it did not in simulation.
method: Data generation: 54 HSSD scenes (49 train / 5 test) imported into Isaac Sim with ray-traced rendering; AIT* with a ReedsShepp state space plans base paths to sampled goals (random side, distance 0.1-0.5 m, angle in {0, ±15, ±30}°); yields 500k trajectories / 7.5M frames, with a camera tilt label per frame.
Goal specification: reference image I_R + object mask M + relative pose C={side S, distance d, angle θ}, so no CAD model or map is needed and the object may be out of view.

RGB-D/LiDAR encoding: frozen MAE-Base tokens (14x14) with depth-derived sinusoidal 3D position embeddings added to RGB patches (optionally with past frames via odometry); 256 LiDAR points grouped into 32 directional-bin tokens via an MLP.

Fusion: a Vision Context Encoder over reference, mask and observation tokens, with an auxiliary mask decoder that tracks the target; goal and robot-footprint radius tokens then enter a Multi-modal Context Encoder.

Base trajectory decoder: autoregressive transformer emitting T=12 waypoints, each as (direction, distance, heading) sub-actions discretized into 30/32/12 bins plus an MLP residual for continuous precision; receding horizon, replanning every 8 steps.
Camera tilt decoder: separate decoder regressing the tilt angle at every step.

Training: behavior cloning with loss L_mask + L_base + L_tilt (150k steps, batch 128, 8 A100), then DAgger on failures; Pure Pursuit tracking for omnidirectional robot, MPC for forklift; runs at 12 Hz on an RTX 3090.

setting.backbone: Transformer (frozen MAE-Base visual encoder + trained context encoders and autoregressive decoders), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: 500k simulated trajectories (7.5M frames) from 49 HSSD scenes in Isaac Sim (3,119 target objects), plus DAgger augmentation; ~500 forklift demos for fine-tuning
setting.observation: Tilting RGB-D camera (1.5 m high) + 2D LiDAR + odometry; reference image with object mask
setting.action_space: Predicted base waypoints (12 waypoints, 0.2 s apart) tracked by Pure Pursuit/MPC, plus continuous camera tilt
setting.privileged: none (baseline uses CAD model and GT occupancy map, AMR does not)

numbers_note: Median error results for simulation (3 cm, 1°) are in the abstract/intro and figures; the error distributions are only in figures. Table 1 gives seen/unseen per-category median errors (e.g. Chair unseen 1.08°/0.04 m). Real-kitchen table gives other objects per hist setting.
results: On unseen HSSD scenes AMR reaches a median error of about 3 cm and 1°, with 95.9% completion when the object is visible (vs 89.0% for the classical FoundationPose+GT-map baseline) and 90.4% when initially out of view. It generalizes to unseen objects with no clear gap, and transfers to a real kitchen with 1.8-3.1 cm errors on most objects (hist=4 succeeded in almost all runs).
limitations: Local navigation only (short-term memory, <10 m); trained only on household scenes so factory or unstructured generalization is uncertain
Assumes a cylindrical robot with a centered camera, limiting legged or complex-shaped robots
Fails with repetitive objects (tracking wrong instance) and ambiguous viewpoints (wrong side)
